attacks.name: Psychic
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon has an organ known as its core. The organ glows in seven colors when Starmie is unleashing its potent psychic powers.

cards.name: Mewtwo

attacks.name: Life Sucker
attacks.text: Heal 20 damage from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: A Pokémon created by recombining Mew's genes. It's said to have the most savage heart among Pokémon.

cards.name: Granbull V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Chomp
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Bull Dash
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.name: Baltoy

attacks.name: Triple Spin
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 20 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: It moves while spinning around on its single foot. Some Baltoy have been seen spinning on their heads.

cards.name: Claydol

attacks.name: Coinciding Figures
attacks.text: If you and your opponent have the same number of Benched Pokémon, this attack does 90 more damage.

cards.flavorText: This mysterious Pokémon started life as an ancient clay figurine made over 20,000 years ago.

cards.name: Duskull

attacks.name: Perplex
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: If it finds bad children who won't listen to their parents, it will spirit them away—or so it's said.

cards.name: Dusclops

attacks.name: Fade to Black
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Its body is entirely hollow. When it opens its mouth, it sucks everything in as if it were a black hole.

cards.name: Dusknoir

abilities.name: Special Transfer
abilities.text: As often as you like during your turn, you may move a Special Energy from 1 of your Pokémon to another of your Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: At the bidding of transmissions from the spirit world, it steals people and Pokémon away. No one knows whether it has a will of its own.

cards.name: Chimecho

attacks.name: Clear Tone
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Special Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: Emitting ultrasonic cries, it floats on winds to travel great distances.

cards.name: Whimsicott V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Fluff Gets in the Way
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokémon is a Basic Pokémon, it can't attack during your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Cotton Guard
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.name: Whimsicott VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Trick Wind
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, they can't play any Pokémon Tool or Special Energy cards from their hand.

attacks.name: Fluffball Star
attacks.text: This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon for each Energy attached to this Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.) (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

cards.name: Sigilyph

attacks.name: Tri Recharge
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. Attach a number of basic Energy cards up to the number of heads from your discard pile to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

attacks.name: Psychic
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Psychic power allows these Pokémon to fly. Some say they were the guardians of an ancient city. Others say they were the guardians' emissaries.

cards.name: Dedenne

attacks.name: Dede-Flash
attacks.text: If your opponent has exactly 1 Prize card remaining, this attack does 60 more damage, and your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Since Dedenne can't generate as much electricity on its own, it steals electricity from outlets or other electric Pokémon.

cards.name: Mimikyu V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Dummy Doll
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may prevent all damage done to this Mimikyu V by attacks from your opponent's Pokémon until the end of your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Jealous Eyes
attacks.text: Put 3 damage counters on your opponent's Active Pokémon for each Prize card your opponent has taken.

cards.name: Mimikyu VMAX
rules: VMAX rule: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Ominous Numbers
attacks.text: Put 4 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like. If you played Acerola's Premonition from your hand during this turn, place 13 damage counters instead.

attacks.name: Max Shadow
attacks.text: Discard a random card from your opponent's hand.

cards.name: Milcery

attacks.name: Lead
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Supporter card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: They say that any patisserie visited by Milcery is guaranteed success and good fortune.

cards.name: Alcremie

abilities.name: Additional Order
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, your turn does not end when you use Café Master.

attacks.name: Rainbow Flavor
attacks.text: This attack does 40 more damage for each type of basic Energy attached to all of your Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: When Alcremie is content, the cream it secretes from its hands becomes sweeter and richer.

cards.name: Hitmontop

attacks.name: Spinning Draw
attacks.text: Draw a card.

cards.flavorText: It launches kicks while spinning. If it spins at high speed, it may bore its way into the ground.

cards.name: Nosepass
cards.flavorText: It hunts without twitching a muscle by pulling in its prey with powerful magnetism. But sometimes it pulls natural enemies in close.

cards.name: Trapinch

attacks.name: Rising Lunge
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Its nest is a sloped, bowl-like pit in the desert. Once something has fallen in, there is no escape.

cards.name: Vibrava
cards.flavorText: The ultrasonic waves it generates by rubbing its two wings together cause severe headaches.

cards.name: Flygon

attacks.name: Desert Pillar
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon hides in the heart of sandstorms it creates and seldom appears where people can see it.

cards.name: Wormadam

attacks.name: Matron's Anger
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each Pokémon in your discard pile.

attacks.name: Bind Down
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

cards.flavorText: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon's body. The cloak is never shed.

cards.name: Riolu
cards.flavorText: It's exceedingly energetic, with enough stamina to keep running all through the night. Taking it for walks can be a challenging experience.

cards.name: Lucario

abilities.name: Roaring Resolve
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may put 2 damage counters on this Pokémon. If you do, search your deck for a Fighting Energy card and attach it to this Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Aura Sphere Volley
attacks.text: Discard all Fighting Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 60 more damage for each card you discarded in this way.

cards.flavorText: It controls waves known as auras, which are powerful enough to pulverize huge rocks. It uses these waves to take down its prey.

cards.name: Throh
cards.flavorText: It performs throwing moves with first-rate skill. Over the course of many battles, Throh's belt grows darker as it absorbs its wearer's sweat.

cards.name: Sawk

attacks.name: Sweep the Leg
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: If you see a Sawk training in the mountains in its single-minded pursuit of strength, it's best to quietly pass by.

cards.name: Golett
cards.flavorText: They were sculpted from clay in ancient times. No one knows why, but some of them are driven to continually line up boulders.

cards.name: Golurk

attacks.name: Big Hand
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each card in your hand.

cards.flavorText: Artillery platforms built into the walls of ancient castles served as perches from which Golurk could fire energy beams.

cards.name: Grimer

attacks.name: Poison Gas
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

cards.flavorText: The wastewater coming from factories is clean these days, so Grimer have nothing to eat. They're said to be on the verge of extinction.

cards.name: Muk

abilities.name: Sludge Street
abilities.text: The Retreat Cost of your opponent's Poisoned Pokémon is Colorless more.

attacks.name: Shrieking Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused and Poisoned.

cards.flavorText: Because they scatter germs everywhere, they've long been targeted for extermination, leading to a steep decline in their population.

cards.name: Sneasel
cards.flavorText: Its paws conceal sharp claws. If attacked, it suddenly extends the claws and startles its enemy.

cards.name: Weavile

attacks.name: Ransack
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. If either of them is heads, your opponent reveals their hand. For each heads, choose a card you find there and put it on the bottom of your opponent's deck in any order.

cards.flavorText: They attack their quarry in packs. Prey as large as Mamoswine easily fall to the teamwork of a group of Weavile.

cards.name: Honchkrow V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Boss Pockets
abilities.text: This Pokémon may have up to 4 Pokémon Tools attached to it. If it loses this Ability, discard Pokémon Tools from it until only 1 remains.

attacks.name: Fearsome Shadow
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand.

cards.name: Spiritomb

attacks.name: Ticking Terror
attacks.text: Until the end of your next turn, the Defending Pokémon's Weakness is now Darkness. (The amount of Weakness doesn't change.)

attacks.name: Cursed Drop
attacks.text: Put 2 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like.

cards.flavorText: Exactly 108 spirits gathered to become this Pokémon. Apparently there are some ill-natured spirits in the mix.

cards.name: Purrloin

attacks.name: Surprise Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

cards.flavorText: It steals things from people just to amuse itself with their frustration. A rivalry exists between this Pokémon and Nickit.

cards.name: Liepard

abilities.name: Trade
abilities.text: You must discard a card from your hand in order to use this Ability. Once during your turn, you may draw 2 cards.

cards.flavorText: Don't be fooled by its gorgeous fur and elegant figure. This is a moody and vicious Pokémon.

cards.name: Impidimp

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.

cards.name: Morgrem
cards.flavorText: When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it's trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.

cards.name: Grimmsnarl

attacks.name: Longhair Shot
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon for each Darkness Energy attached to this Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.

cards.name: Morpeko V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Gnaw and Run
attacks.text: You may switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Hangry Spike
attacks.text: If you played Marnie's Pride from your hand during this turn, this attack does 120 more damage.

cards.name: Aggron V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Rock Slide
attacks.text: This attack also does 30 damage to 2 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Merciless Strike
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon already has any damage counters on it, this attack does 150 more damage.

cards.name: Aggron VMAX
rules: VMAX rule: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Cracking Stomp
attacks.text: Discard the top card of your opponent's deck.

attacks.name: Max Take Down
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.name: Wormadam

attacks.name: Matron's Anger
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each Pokémon in your discard pile.

cards.flavorText: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon's body. The cloak is never shed.

cards.name: Probopass

attacks.name: Magnetic Tension
attacks.text: Switch 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon with their Active Pokémon. This attack does 40 damage to the new Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Iron Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 20 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: It uses three small units to catch prey and battle enemies. The main body mostly just gives orders.

cards.name: Heatran

attacks.name: Guard Claw
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Iron Hammer
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has any Fire Energy attached, this attack does 80 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Boiling blood, like magma, circulates through its body. It makes its dwelling place in volcanic caves.

cards.name: Escavalier

abilities.name: Miraculous Armor
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 100 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon V (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Pike
attacks.text: This attack also does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: They use shells they've stolen from Shelmet to arm and protect themselves. They're very popular Pokémon in the Galar region.

cards.name: Klink
cards.flavorText: The two minigears that compose this Pokémon are closer than twins. They mesh well only with each other.

cards.name: Klang

attacks.name: Guard Press
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: When Klang goes all out, the minigear links up perfectly with the outer part of the big gear, and this Pokémon's rotation speed increases sharply.

cards.name: Klinklang

abilities.name: Gear Wall
abilities.text: Your Basic Pokémon take 20 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Tumbling Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 90 more damage.

cards.flavorText: From its spikes, it launches powerful blasts of electricity. Its red core contains an enormous amount of energy.

cards.name: Zamazenta V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Regal Stance
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may discard your hand and draw 5 cards. If you use this Ability, your turn ends.

attacks.name: Revenge Blast
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken.

cards.name: Flygon V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Draconic Impulse
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Pokémon VMAX, this attack does 160 more damage, and discard 3 Energy from this Pokémon.

cards.name: Gible
cards.flavorText: Gible prefers to stay in narrow holes in the sides of caves heated by geothermal energy. This way, Gible can stay warm even during a blizzard.

cards.name: Gabite
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon emits ultrasonic waves from a protrusion on either side of its head to probe pitch-dark caves.

cards.name: Garchomp

abilities.name: Sonic Slip
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may prevent all damage from and effects of attacks from your opponent's Pokémon done to this Pokémon until the end of your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Dragonblade
attacks.text: Discard the top 2 cards of your deck.

cards.flavorText: Garchomp makes its home in volcanic mountains. It flies through the sky as fast as a jet airplane, hunting down as much prey as it can.

cards.name: Axew

attacks.name: Ultra Evolution
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, search your deck for a Haxorus and put it onto this Axew to evolve it. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: These Pokémon nest in the ground and use their tusks to crush hard berries. Crushing berries is also how they test each other's strength.

cards.name: Fraxure
cards.flavorText: After battle, this Pokémon carefully sharpens its tusks on river rocks. It needs to take care of its tusks—if one breaks, it will never grow back.

cards.name: Haxorus

attacks.name: Wild Axe
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: Its resilient tusks are its pride and joy. It licks up dirt to take in the minerals it needs to keep its tusks in top condition.

cards.name: Druddigon

attacks.name: Revenge
attacks.text: If any of your Pokémon were Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon during their last turn, this attack does 120 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Druddigon are vicious and cunning. They take up residence in nests dug out by other Pokémon, treating the stolen nests as their own lairs.

cards.name: Dracovish V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Slosh 'n' Crash
attacks.text: Before doing damage, discard all Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Active Pokémon. If you discarded a Pokémon Tool in this way, this attack does 120 more damage.

attacks.name: Dragon Strike
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Dragon Strike.

cards.name: Farfetch'd

attacks.name: Leek Lash
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The stalk this Pokémon carries in its wings serves as a sword to cut down opponents. In a dire situation, the stalk can also serve as food.

cards.name: Castform

attacks.name: Double Draw
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

attacks.name: Hurricane
attacks.text: Move a basic Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Its form changes depending on the weather. The rougher conditions get, the rougher Castform's disposition!

cards.name: Starly

attacks.name: Claw
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

cards.flavorText: They flock around mountains and fields, chasing after bug Pokémon. Their singing is noisy and annoying.

cards.name: Staravia
cards.flavorText: It lives in forests and fields. Squabbles over territory occur when flocks collide.

cards.name: Staraptor

attacks.name: Strong Breeze
attacks.text: Your opponent shuffles their Active Pokémon and all attached cards into their deck.

attacks.name: Spinning Bird
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: When Staravia evolve into Staraptor, they leave the flock to live alone. They have sturdy wings.

cards.name: Bidoof
cards.flavorText: It constantly gnaws on logs and rocks to whittle down its front teeth. It nests alongside water.

cards.name: Bibarel

abilities.name: Industrious Incisors
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may draw cards until you have 5 cards in your hand.

attacks.name: Tail Smash
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

cards.flavorText: It makes its nest by damming streams with bark and mud. It is known as an industrious worker.

cards.name: Arceus V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Trinity Charge
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 basic Energy cards and attach them to your Pokémon V in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.name: Arceus VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Starbirth
abilities.text: During your turn, you may search your deck for up to 2 cards and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Trinity Nova
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 basic Energy cards and attach them to your Pokémon V in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.name: Minccino

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.

cards.name: Cinccino

attacks.name: Triple Axel
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 50 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: Its body secretes oil that this Pokémon spreads over its nest as a coating to protect it from dust. Cinccino won't tolerate even a speck of the stuff.

cards.name: Tornadus

abilities.name: Sudden Cyclone
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench, you may have your opponent switch their Active Pokémon with 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

cards.name: Hawlucha

attacks.name: Showboating Pose
attacks.text: Attach up to 2 basic Energy cards from your discard pile to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Cross-Cut
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is an Evolution Pokémon, this attack does 30 more damage.

cards.flavorText: It drives its opponents to exhaustion with its agile maneuvers, then ends the fight with a flashy finishing move.

cards.name: Drampa V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Spike Draw
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

attacks.name: Dragon Pulse
attacks.text: Discard the top 2 cards of your deck.

cards.name: Acerola's Premonition
rules: Your opponent reveals their hand, and you draw a card for each Trainer card you find there.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Barry
rules: Draw 3 cards.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Blunder Policy
rules: If the Pokémon this card is attached to uses an attack, if you flip any coins for the damage or effect of that attack, and if any of them are tails, draw 3 cards at the end of your turn.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
Attach a Pokémon Tool to 1 of your Pokémon that doesn't already have a Pokémon Tool attached.

cards.name: Boss's Orders
rules: Switch 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon with their Active Pokémon.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Café Master
rules: Choose up to 3 of your Benched Pokémon. For each of those Pokémon, search your deck for a different type of basic Energy card and attach it to that Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck. Your turn ends.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Cheren's Care
rules: Put 1 of your Colorless Pokémon that has any damage counters on it and all attached cards into your hand.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Choice Belt
rules: The attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon V (before applying Weakness and Resistance).
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
Attach a Pokémon Tool to 1 of your Pokémon that doesn't already have a Pokémon Tool attached.

cards.name: Cleansing Gloves
rules: The attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Psychic Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
Attach a Pokémon Tool to 1 of your Pokémon that doesn't already have a Pokémon Tool attached.

cards.name: Collapsed Stadium
rules: Each player can't have more than 4 Benched Pokémon. If a player has 5 or more Benched Pokémon, they discard Benched Pokémon until they have 4 Pokémon on the Bench. The player who played this card discards first. If more than one effect changes the number of Benched Pokémon allowed, use the smaller number.

cards.name: Cynthia's Ambition
rules: Draw cards until you have 5 cards in your hand. If any of your Pokémon were Knocked Out during your opponent's last turn, draw cards until you have 8 cards in your hand instead.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Fresh Water Set
rules: Heal 20 damage from each of your Pokémon.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

cards.name: Friends in Galar
rules: Draw 3 cards.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Gloria
rules: Search your deck for up to 3 Basic Pokémon that don't have a Rule Box and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck. (Pokémon V, Pokémon-GX, etc. have Rule Boxes.)
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Hunting Gloves
rules: The attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Dragon Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
Attach a Pokémon Tool to 1 of your Pokémon that doesn't already have a Pokémon Tool attached.

cards.name: Kindler
rules: You can use this card only if you discard a Fire Energy card from your hand. Look at the top 7 cards of your deck and put up to 2 of them into your hand. Shuffle the other cards back into your deck.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Magma Basin
rules: Once during each player's turn, that player may attach a Fire Energy card from their discard pile to 1 of their Benched Fire Pokémon. If a player attached Energy to a Pokémon in this way, put 2 damage counters on that Pokémon.

cards.name: Marnie's Pride
rules: Attach a basic Energy card from your discard pile to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Pot Helmet
rules: If the Pokémon this card is attached to doesn't have a Rule Box, it takes 30 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance). (Pokémon V, Pokémon-GX, etc. have Rule Boxes.)
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
Attach a Pokémon Tool to 1 of your Pokémon that doesn't already have a Pokémon Tool attached.

cards.name: Professor's Research
rules: Discard your hand and draw 7 cards.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Roseanne's Backup
rules:
Choose 1 or more:
• Shuffle a Pokémon from your discard pile into your deck.
• Shuffle a Pokémon Tool card from your discard pile into your deck.
• Shuffle a Stadium card from your discard pile into your deck.
• Shuffle an Energy card from your discard pile into your deck.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Team Yell's Cheer
rules: Shuffle up to 3 in any combination of Pokémon and Supporter cards, except for Team Yell's Cheer, from your discard pile into your deck.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

cards.name: Ultra Ball
rules: You can use this card only if you discard 2 other cards from your hand. Search your deck for a Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

cards.name: Double Turbo Energy
rules: As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides ColorlessColorless Energy. The attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 20 less damage to your opponent's Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.name: Shaymin V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Revenge Blast
attacks.text: This attack does 40 more damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken.

cards.name: Charizard V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Incinerate
attacks.text: Before doing damage, discard all Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Charizard V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Incinerate
attacks.text: Before doing damage, discard all Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Lumineon V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Luminous Sign
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may search your deck for a Supporter card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Aqua Return
attacks.text: Shuffle this Pokémon and all attached cards into your deck.

cards.name: Lumineon V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

cards.name: Flareon

abilities.text: If this Pokémon has a Memory Capsule attached, Grass Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Abilities.

cards.flavorText: Once it has stored up enough heat, this Pokémon's body temperature can reach up to 1,700 degrees Fahrenheit.

cards.name: Vaporeon

abilities.name: Torrential Awakening
abilities.text: If this Pokémon has a Memory Capsule attached, Fire Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Abilities.

cards.flavorText: When Vaporeon's fins begin to vibrate, it is a sign that rain will come within a few hours.

cards.name: Octillery

cards.flavorText: It traps enemies with its suction-cupped tentacles, then smashes them with its rock-hard head.

cards.name: Jolteon

abilities.name: Thunderous Awakening
abilities.text: If this Pokémon has a Memory Capsule attached, Water Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Abilities.

cards.flavorText: If it is angered or startled, the fur all over its body bristles like sharp needles that pierce foes.

cards.name: Zekrom

attacks.name: Wild Shock
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 60 damage to itself. Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: When the interior part of its tail spins like a motor, Zekrom can generate many bolts of lightning to blast its surroundings.

cards.name: Dusknoir

abilities.name: Spectral Breach
abilities.text: All Special Energy attached to Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's) provide Colorless Energy and have no other effect.

cards.flavorText: At the bidding of transmissions from the spirit world, it steals people and Pokémon away. No one knows whether it has a will of its own.

cards.name: Dedenne

attacks.name: Dede-Flash
attacks.text: If your opponent has exactly 1 Prize card remaining, this attack does 60 more damage, and your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Since Dedenne can't generate as much electricity on its own, it steals electricity from outlets or other electric Pokémon.

cards.name: Alcremie

attacks.name: Rainbow Flavor

cards.flavorText: When Alcremie is content, the cream it secretes from its hands becomes sweeter and richer.

cards.flavorText: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.

cards.flavorText: Identifiable by its eerie howls, people a long time ago thought it was the grim reaper and feared it.

cards.flavorText: Thanks to its unstable genetic makeup, this special Pokémon conceals many different possible evolutions.

cards.flavorText: It knows the forest inside and out. If it comes across a wounded Pokémon, Oranguru will gather medicinal herbs to treat it.

cards.name: Hisuian Voltorb

attacks.name: Cheerful Charge
attacks.text: You can use this attack only if you go second, and only during your first turn. Choose up to 2 of your Benched Pokémon. For each of those Pokémon, search your deck for a basic Energy card and attach it to that Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.

cards.name: Hisuian Electrode

attacks.name: Triple Draw
attacks.text: Draw 3 cards.

cards.flavorText: The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.

cards.name: Scyther
cards.flavorText: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.

cards.name: Scyther

attacks.name: Quick Blow
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.

cards.flavorText: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.

cards.name: Yanma
cards.flavorText: Its frail wings are so thin that one can see clear through them. However, during flight these wings exhibit the power to churn air with force enough to launch a house skyward.

cards.name: Yanmega

attacks.name: Wide Wing
attacks.text: If you have more cards in your hand than your opponent, this attack does 80 more damage.

cards.flavorText: This six-legged Pokémon is easily capable of transporting an adult in flight. The wings on its tail help it stay balanced.

cards.name: Heracross

attacks.name: Overhead Throw
attacks.text: This attack also does 30 damage to 1 of your Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon has an unparalleled horn. Heracross itself demonstrates tremendous power—it's capable of throwing several people trained in the traditional arts of war at once.

cards.name: Kricketot

attacks.name: Trip Over
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

cards.flavorText: When its antennae hit each other, it sounds like the music of a xylophone.

cards.name: Kricketune

abilities.name: Swelling Tune
abilities.text: Your Grass Pokémon in play, except any Kricketune, get +40 HP. You can't apply more than 1 Swelling Tune Ability at a time.

cards.flavorText: It uses its cutlass-like arms to produce sound, the melody of which varies from individual to individual. It is a worthwhile endeavor to seek out one's favorite tunes.

cards.name: Combee

attacks.name: Honey Courier
attacks.text: Search your deck for an Item card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: The members of the trio spend all their time together. Each one has a slightly different taste in nectar.

cards.name: Vespiquen

attacks.name: Honey Rush
attacks.text: Reveal any number of Sweet Honey cards from your hand. This attack does 60 damage for each card you revealed in this way.

cards.flavorText: It skillfully commands its grubs in battles with its enemies. The grubs are willing to risk their lives to defend Vespiquen.

cards.name: Leafeon

attacks.name: Energy Garden
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 basic Energy cards of different types and attach them to your Pokémon in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Leafy Cyclone
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

cards.flavorText: Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.

cards.name: Shaymin

attacks.name: Encouraging Gift
attacks.text: You can use this attack only if you go second, and only during your first turn. Search your deck for up to 3 cards and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: When the turning of seasons brings the cruel winter to its end and the joyous people give thanks to the heavens, Shaymin appears and covers the withered land with flowers.

cards.name: Petilil

attacks.name: Spin Turn
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: The leaves on its head are highly valued for medicinal purposes. Dry the leaves in the sun, boil them, and then drink the bitter decoction for remarkably effective relief from fatigue.

cards.name: Hisuian Lilligant

attacks.name: Twister Lutz
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage to each of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.) Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

cards.name: Hisuian Lilligant V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Dance Gracefully
attacks.text: Draw cards until you have 6 cards in your hand.

cards.name: Hisuian Lilligant VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Star Perfume
abilities.text: During your turn, you may search your deck for up to 5 in any combination of Grass Pokémon and Grass Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Parallel Spin
attacks.text: You may put an Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand. If you do, this attack does 100 more damage.

cards.name: Rowlet

attacks.name: Jump On
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Flies noiselessly on delicate wings. It has mastered the art of deftly launching dagger-sharp feathers from those same wings.

cards.name: Dartrix
cards.flavorText: Regularly basks in sunlight to gather power—presumably due to the frigid climate. Nonetheless, the edges of the blade quills set into its wings are keen as ever.

cards.name: Ponyta
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon live in herds out in the grassland. Newborn foals lack their fiery manes, which will develop about an hour after birth.

cards.name: Rapidash

attacks.name: Ring of Fire
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned. During your opponent's next turn, that Pokémon can't retreat.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.

cards.name: Cyndaquil

attacks.name: Charge Energy
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 basic Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.

cards.name: Quilava
cards.flavorText: This creature's fur is most mysterious—it is wholly impervious to the burning touch of flame. Should Quilava turn its back to you, take heed! Such a posture indicates a forthcoming attack.

cards.name: Heatran V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Heat Burn
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

attacks.name: Magma Fall
attacks.text: If you have a Stadium in play, this attack does 90 more damage.

cards.name: Heatran VMAX
rules: VMAX rule: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Magma Gain
abilities.text: Once during your turn, if you have a Stadium in play, you may heal 50 damage from this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Max Heat Burst
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

cards.name: Radiant Heatran
rules: Radiant Pokémon Rule: You can't have more than 1 Radiant Pokémon in your deck.

attacks.name: Raging Blast
attacks.text: This attack does 70 damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Boiling blood, like magma, circulates through its body. It makes its dwelling place in volcanic caves.

cards.name: Psyduck

attacks.name: Spacing Out
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, heal 10 damage from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Suffers perpetual headaches. If the agony grows too great, Psyduck's latent power erupts, contrary to Psyduck's intent. Ergo, I am exploring ways to ease the pain.

cards.name: Golduck

attacks.name: Entangled Dive
attacks.text: Discard each player's Active Pokémon and all attached cards. (You choose a new Active Pokémon first.)

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon lives in gently flowing rivers. It paddles through the water with its long limbs, putting its graceful swimming skills on display.

cards.name: Starmie V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Swift
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance, or by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Energy Spiral
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage for each Energy attached to all of your opponent's Pokémon.

cards.name: Swinub

attacks.name: Icy Wind
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

cards.flavorText: Swinub excels at sniffing out mushrooms buried beneath grass or snow. Since ancient times, the people of Hisui have often relied upon this skill.

cards.name: Piloswine

attacks.name: Blizzard
attacks.text: This attack also does 10 damage to each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: If it charges at an enemy, the hairs on its back stand up straight. It is very sensitive to sound.

cards.name: Mamoswine

attacks.name: Blizzard
attacks.text: This attack also does 10 damage to each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Iceberg Press
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon. During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't attack.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can be spotted in wall paintings from as far back as 10,000 years ago. For a while, it was thought to have gone extinct.

cards.name: Mantine

attacks.name: Borne Ashore
attacks.text: Put a Basic Pokémon from either player's discard pile onto that player's Bench.

cards.flavorText: This calm and gentle Pokémon swims gracefully through the sea. After building speed, it can leap out of the water. It is often misidentified as a bird Pokémon due to this behavior.

cards.name: Barboach
cards.flavorText: Makes its home in swamps with murky water. The poor visibility hides this Pokémon from predators, and the slime on its body makes grasping it difficult.

cards.name: Whiscash

attacks.name: Thrash
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this Pokémon also does 60 damage to itself. If heads, this attack does 60 more damage.

cards.flavorText: It makes its nest at the bottom of swamps. It will eat anything—if it is alive, Whiscash will eat it.

cards.name: Regice

attacks.name: Regi Gate
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Blizzard Bind
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokémon is a Pokémon V, it can't attack during your opponent's next turn.

cards.flavorText: With cold air that can reach temperatures as low as −328 degrees Fahrenheit, Regice instantly freezes any creature that approaches it.

cards.name: Glaceon

attacks.name: Frost Wall
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from Evolution Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.

cards.name: Origin Forme Palkia V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Rule the Region
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Stadium card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Hydro Break
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

cards.name: Origin Forme Palkia VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Star Portal
abilities.text: During your turn, you may attach up to 3 Water Energy cards from your discard pile to your Water Pokémon in any way you like. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Subspace Swell
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage for each Benched Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's).

cards.name: Oshawott
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon from the Unova region uses the shell on its belly as a weapon to cut down its foes. Thus, I've conferred upon this shell the name "scalchop.".

cards.name: Dewott

attacks.name: Razor Shell
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Its exquisite double-scalchop technique is likely the result of daily training, and it can send even masters of the blade fleeing in defeat.

cards.name: Hisuian Basculin

attacks.name: Gather the Crew
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: Though it differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor—this one is gentle—I have categorized it as a regional form given the vast array of shared qualities.

cards.name: Hisuian Basculegion

attacks.name: Grudge Dive
attacks.text: If any of your Pokémon were Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon during their last turn, this attack does 90 more damage, and your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

cards.name: Keldeo

attacks.name: Line Force
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage for each of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: When it is resolute, its body fills with power and it becomes swifter. Its jumps are then too fast to follow.

cards.name: Radiant Greninja
rules: Radiant Pokémon Rule: You can't have more than 1 Radiant Pokémon in your deck.

abilities.name: Concealed Cards
abilities.text: You must discard an Energy card from your hand in order to use this Ability. Once during your turn, you may draw 2 cards.

attacks.name: Moonlight Shuriken
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 90 damage to 2 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: It appears and vanishes with a ninja's grace. It toys with its enemies using swift movements, while slicing them with throwing stars of sharpest water.

cards.name: Bergmite
cards.flavorText: Lives on mountains blanketed in perennial snow. It freezes water vapor in the air to make the ice helmet that it dons for defense.

cards.name: Hisuian Avalugg

abilities.name: Massive Ice
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Mountain Gale
attacks.text: If a Stadium is in play, this attack does 120 more damage. Then, discard that Stadium.

cards.flavorText: The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.

cards.name: Galarian Mr. Rime V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Surprising Hand
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 Item cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Customized Cane
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has a Pokémon Tool attached, this attack does 90 more damage.

cards.name: Luxray V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Fang Snipe
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. Discard a Trainer card you find there.

attacks.name: Radiating Pulse
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon. Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.name: Regieleki

attacks.name: Electromagnetic Sonar
attacks.text: Put a Trainer card from your discard pile into your hand.

attacks.name: Targeted Bolt
attacks.text: Discard 2 Lightning Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 120 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It's said that removing the rings on Regieleki's body will unleash the Pokémon's latent power.

cards.name: Hisuian Typhlosion

abilities.name: Supernatural Orb
abilities.text: You must discard a Psychic Energy card from your hand in order to use this Ability. Once during your turn, you may make your opponent's Active Pokémon Burned and Confused.

attacks.name: Shadow Bind
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

cards.flavorText: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.

cards.name: Hisuian Typhlosion V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Singe
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

attacks.name: Petrifying Flame
attacks.text: Choose a random card from your opponent's hand. Your opponent reveals that card and shuffles it into their deck.

cards.name: Hisuian Typhlosion VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Hollow Flame
attacks.text: Put 3 damage counters on your opponent's Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

attacks.name: Shimmering Star
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon has exactly 4 damage counters on it, that Pokémon is Knocked Out. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

cards.name: Togepi

abilities.name: Touch of Happiness
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may heal 10 damage from your Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: This ovate creature is frequently mistaken for a moving egg when encountered out in the fields or in the mountains. Its guileless smile soothes the soul.

cards.name: Togetic

abilities.name: Voice of Happiness
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may heal 30 damage from your Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: They say that it will appear before kindhearted, caring people and shower them with happiness.

cards.name: Togekiss

abilities.name: Shine of Happiness
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may heal 90 damage from your Active Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: These Pokémon are never seen anywhere near conflict or turmoil. In recent times, they've hardly been seen at all.

cards.name: Misdreavus
cards.flavorText: It conceals itself in darkness, sending chills up travelers' spines with its childlike weeping. As it observes the frightened travelers with glee, the red orbs upon its chest let off an eerie light.

cards.name: Mismagius

attacks.name: Ominous Prose
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. If they have 4 or more cards in their hand, choose all but 3, and your opponent shuffles the chosen cards into their deck.

attacks.name: Psybeam
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: Its muttered curses can cause awful headaches or terrifying visions that torment others.

cards.name: Ralts

attacks.name: Teleportation Burst
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Tends to prefer people with a chipper disposition to those who are gloomy, but it has shown no discrimination with regard to age or gender. Needs more research.

cards.name: Kirlia

attacks.name: Teleportation Burst
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: If its Trainer becomes happy, it overflows with energy, dancing joyously while spinning about.

cards.name: Gallade

abilities.name: Buddy Catch
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for a Supporter card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Swirling Slice
attacks.text: Move an Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: True to its honorable-warrior image, it uses the blades on its elbows only in defense of something or someone.

cards.name: Drifloon

attacks.name: Triple Spin
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: Said to lure away young children and carry them off to the afterlife. Some whisper that Drifloon are formed of reincarnated human souls, but these rumors are as yet unconfirmed.

cards.name: Drifblim

attacks.name: Spooky Balloon
attacks.text: Put 2 damage counters on 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Some say this Pokémon is a collection of souls burdened with regrets, silently drifting through the dusk.

cards.name: Uxie

attacks.name: Wise Guidance
attacks.text: Search your deck for a card and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.flavorText: It is said that its emergence gave humans the intelligence to improve their quality of life.

cards.name: Mesprit

abilities.name: Mental Shroud
abilities.text: If you have Uxie and Azelf in play, each of your Pokémon has no Weakness.

cards.flavorText: It sleeps at the bottom of a lake. Its spirit is said to leave its body to fly on the lake's surface.

cards.name: Azelf

attacks.name: Mind Bend
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

cards.flavorText: It is thought that Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf all came from the same egg.

cards.name: Diancie

abilities.name: Princess's Curtain
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, whenever your opponent plays a Supporter card from their hand, prevent all effects of that card done to your Benched Basic Pokémon.

attacks.name: Spike Draw
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

cards.flavorText: It can instantly create many diamonds by compressing the carbon in the air between its hands.

cards.name: Wyrdeer

abilities.name: Hurried Gait
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may draw a card.

attacks.name: Extrasensory
attacks.text: If you have the same number of cards in your hand as your opponent, this attack does 80 more damage.

cards.flavorText: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

cards.name: Hisuian Growlithe

attacks.name: Defensive Posture
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks.

cards.flavorText: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

cards.name: Hisuian Arcanine

attacks.name: Scorching Horn
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has any Fire Energy attached, this attack does 80 more damage, and your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

cards.flavorText: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

cards.name: Machamp V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Revenge Buster
attacks.text: If your Benched Pokémon have any damage counters on them, this attack does 50 more damage.

cards.name: Machamp VMAX
rules: VMAX rule: When your Pokémon VMAX is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 3 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Revenge Buster
attacks.text: If your Benched Pokémon have any damage counters on them, this attack does 140 more damage.

attacks.name: G-Max Chi Strike
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use G-Max Chi Strike.

cards.name: Sudowoodo

abilities.name: Vamoose
abilities.text: If this Pokémon has any damage counters on it, it has no Retreat Cost.

attacks.name: Double-Edge
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.

cards.name: Regirock

attacks.name: Regi Gate
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Giga Impact
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

cards.flavorText: Every bit of Regirock's body is made of stone. As parts of its body erode, this Pokémon sticks rocks to itself to repair what's been lost.

cards.name: Cranidos

attacks.name: Stone Edge
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 40 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Its hard skull is its distinguishing feature. It snapped trees by headbutting them, and then it fed on their ripe berries.

cards.name: Rampardos

attacks.name: Jurassic Hammer
attacks.text: If your opponent has 3 or fewer cards in their hand, this attack does nothing.

cards.flavorText: This ancient Pokémon used headbutts skillfully. Its brain was really small, so some theories suggest that its stupidity led to its extinction.

cards.name: Lucario V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Crushing Punch
attacks.text: Discard a Special Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Hippopotas
cards.flavorText: Though large and languid, Hippopotas is difficult to detect due to its tendency to burrow into and lurk beneath the soil. When agitated or excited, it expels sand from its nostrils.

cards.name: Hippowdon

attacks.name: Sand Breath
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Stones can get stuck in the ports on their bodies. Dwebble help dislodge such stones, so Hippowdon look after these Pokémon.

cards.name: Radiant Hawlucha
rules: Radiant Pokémon Rule: You can't have more than 1 Radiant Pokémon in your deck.

abilities.name: Big Match
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, your Pokémon's attacks do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon VMAX (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.flavorText: It drives its opponents to exhaustion with its agile maneuvers, then ends the fight with a flashy finishing move.

cards.name: Hisuian Decidueye

attacks.name: Piercing Claw
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Direct Arrow
attacks.text: This attack does 80 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

cards.flavorText: The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye's feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui's extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.

cards.name: Hisuian Decidueye V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Mountain Hunt
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 cards and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Close-Quarters Shooting
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Hisuian Decidueye VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Star of Fortune
abilities.text: During your turn, you may draw cards until you have 8 cards in your hand. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Somersault Feathers
attacks.text: You may discard up to 3 Energy cards from your hand. This attack does 30 more damage for each card you discarded in this way.

cards.name: Kleavor

attacks.name: Rout
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Rocky Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 50 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

cards.name: Kleavor

attacks.name: Timber Cleave
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. If both of them are heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is Knocked Out.

attacks.name: Berserker Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

cards.name: Kleavor V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Axe Slash
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon. If you do, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Hisuian Qwilfish
cards.flavorText: Fishers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it sprays poison from its spines, getting it everywhere. A different form of Qwilfish lives in other regions.

cards.name: Hisuian Qwilfish

attacks.name: Spiny Rush
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

cards.flavorText: Fishers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it sprays poison from its spines, getting it everywhere. A different form of Qwilfish lives in other regions.

cards.name: Hisuian Overqwil

attacks.name: Tormenting Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned. During Pokémon Checkup, put 5 damage counters on that Pokémon instead of 1.

attacks.name: Pinning
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

cards.flavorText: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname "sea fiend." It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

cards.name: Hisuian Overqwil

attacks.name: Dirty Press
attacks.text: If you have at least 3 Darkness Energy in play, this attack does 90 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname "sea fiend." It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

cards.name: Hisuian Sneasel
cards.flavorText: Its sturdy, curved claws are ideal for traversing precipitous cliffs. From the tips of these claws drips a venom that infiltrates the nerves of any prey caught in Sneasel's grasp.

cards.name: Hisuian Sneasler

abilities.name: Carry and Climb
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, your Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost is ColorlessColorless less.

cards.flavorText: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

cards.name: Hisuian Sneasler V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Poison Claws
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Dire Claw
attacks.text: This attack does 80 damage for each Special Condition affecting your opponent's Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Poochyena

attacks.name: Slight Intrusion
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 10 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: It has a very tenacious nature. Its acute sense of smell lets it chase a chosen prey without ever losing track.

cards.name: Mightyena

abilities.name: Hustle Bark
abilities.text: If your opponent has any Pokémon VMAX in play, this Pokémon's attacks cost ColorlessColorlessColorless less.

attacks.name: Wild Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 50 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: It chases down prey in a pack of around ten. They defeat foes with perfectly coordinated teamwork.

cards.name: Absol

attacks.name: Swirling Disaster
attacks.text: This attack does 10 damage to each of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Claw Rend
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon already has any damage counters on it, this attack does 70 more damage.

cards.flavorText: Swift as the wind, Absol races through fields and mountains. Its curved, bow-like horn is acutely sensitive to the warning signs of natural disasters.

cards.name: Darkrai V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Dark Void
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

cards.name: Darkrai VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Star Abyss
abilities.text: During your turn, you may put up to 2 Item cards from your discard pile into your hand. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Dark Pulse
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Darkness Energy attached to all of your Pokémon.

cards.name: Hisuian Samurott

abilities.name: Wily Stance
abilities.text: You must discard a card from your hand in order to use this Ability. Once during your turn, you may draw 3 cards.

attacks.name: Dark Mastery
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage for each Energy attached to all of your Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon's evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.

cards.name: Hisuian Samurott V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Basket Crash
attacks.text: Discard up to 2 Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Pokémon.

attacks.name: Shadow Slash
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

cards.name: Hisuian Samurott VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Moon Cleave Star
abilities.text: During your turn, you may put 4 damage counters on 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (You can't use more than 1 VSTAR Power in a game.)

attacks.name: Merciless Blade
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon already has any damage counters on it, this attack does 110 more damage.

cards.name: Nickit
cards.flavorText: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.

cards.name: Thievul

abilities.name: Baffling
abilities.text: If your opponent has 2 or fewer Prize cards remaining, whenever your opponent plays a Supporter card from their hand, prevent all effects of that card done to your Benched Pokémon V.

cards.flavorText: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.

cards.name: Magnemite

attacks.name: Magnetic Catch
attacks.text: Shuffle up to 3 Metal Energy cards from your discard pile into your deck.

cards.flavorText: A bizarre Pokémon with but a single eye embedded in an iron sphere. I suspect this creature levitates due to the magnetism it emits from its arms, which resemble horseshoe-shaped magnets.

cards.name: Magneton

attacks.name: Bounce Back
attacks.text: Your opponent switches their Active Pokémon with 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is three Magnemite that have linked together. Magneton sends out powerful radio waves to study its surroundings.

cards.name: Magnezone

abilities.name: Giga Magnet
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may look at the top 6 cards of your deck and attach any number of Metal Energy cards you find there to your Pokémon in any way you like. Shuffle the other cards back into your deck.

cards.flavorText: Some say that Magnezone receives signals from space via the antenna on its head and that it's being controlled by some mysterious being.

cards.name: Registeel

attacks.name: Regi Gate
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Heavy Slam
attacks.text: This attack does 50 less damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

cards.flavorText: Registeel's body is made of a strange material that is flexible enough to stretch and shrink but also more durable than any metal.

cards.name: Shieldon

attacks.name: Hard Headbutt
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage from and effects of attacks done to this Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Although its fossils can be found in layers of primeval rock, nothing but its face has ever been discovered.

cards.name: Bastiodon

abilities.name: Primal Fortress
abilities.text: Your Pokémon take 30 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon V (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Iron Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is from roughly 100 million years ago. Its terrifyingly tough face is harder than steel.

cards.name: Bronzor

attacks.name: Metal Press
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

cards.flavorText: Floats using a mysterious energy. The pattern engraved upon its back is held as sacred and can sometimes be found in imagery from ancient cemeteries and other such timeworn places.

cards.name: Bronzong

abilities.name: Heatproof
abilities.text: Prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from your opponent's Fire Pokémon.

cards.flavorText: Some believe it to be a deity that summons rain clouds. When angered, it lets out a warning cry that rings out like the tolling of a bell.

cards.name: Origin Forme Dialga V
rules: V rule: When your Pokémon V is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Metal Coating
attacks.text: Attach up to 2 Metal Energy cards from your discard pile to this Pokémon.

cards.name: Origin Forme Dialga VSTAR
rules: VSTAR rule: When your Pokémon VSTAR is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Metal Blast
attacks.text: This attack does 40 more damage for each Metal Energy attached to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Star Chronos

attacks.name: Continuous Slap
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 40 damage for each heads.
